block.comment: Pan signal D9 (OC1A), tilt D10 (OC1B): Timer1 generates both servo pulse trains. Use a suitable servo supply and common ground. Light sensor divider output goes to A0; arrange the mechanics so these angles are clear.
Two servos share Timer1 with the same 20 ms frame. No Timer1 stepper or Timer1 audio in this example.

Select this board and port, upload, open Plotter at 115200 baud and press Start. Start sends START + newline. Stop sends STOP + newline. Starting again resets this demonstration and sends its header again.
Five-byte command buffer. Only the small incoming command is stored on the board; Plotter stores charts and images on the computer.
This is an ordinary Serial text message stored in Flash. Click it to edit formatted JSON. The computer creates instruments and computes derived fields; this sketch sends only input values.

Reusable command reader. Plotter sends START + newline (byte 10) or STOP + newline. Keep at most five bytes; ignore CR (13), reject longer lines, and act only on a complete matching word. Partial commands never start the sketch. No String allocation and no waiting for input.
Use elapsed milliseconds instead of delay. The command reader remains responsive between updates; unsigned subtraction also works when millis wraps.

32×24 photocell scanner. Start positions the servos, then the first measurement waits 80 ms. Each sample replaces one PC image pixel and adds a chart point; the Arduino stores no image. A completed raster starts again without clearing old pixels. Increase the interval if your mechanics need more settling time. Upload first, then click Start in Plotter. It stays idle until START; STOP ends data without resetting the board. Read command handling in the collapsed function.
